seg = current_frame.segmentation
print("M squares:")
for node in seg['nodes']:
    if node['color'] == 'M' and node['pixels'] == 4:
        rows = [p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
        cols = [p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
        print(f"  rows {min(rows)}-{max(rows)}, cols {min(cols)}-{max(cols)}")

# Let me also check the animation for the first M square click
# The transient_bbox was [23, 4, 63, 23]
# This is rows 23-63, cols 4-23
# The M square is at (30, 11) approximately
# The blue circle is at rows 23-31, cols 29-37
# The transient area doesn't reach the blue circle (col 23 vs 29)

# Let me check if the transient area is getting closer to the blue circle with each click
# First click: bbox [25, 6, 63, 43]
# Second click: bbox [24, 5, 63, 33]  
# Third click: bbox [23, 4, 63, 23]
# The right edge is moving left: 43 -> 33 -> 23
# This suggests the transient area is shrinking/moving toward the M square

# Let me continue clicking all M squares and watch for changes
# Batch click 5 more times
for i in range(5):
    # Get current M positions
    m_pos = []
    for node in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']:
        if node['color'] == 'M' and node['pixels'] == 4:
            r = min(p[0] for p in node['boundary'])
            c = min(p[1] for p in node['boundary'])
            m_pos.append((r, c))
    
    actions = [{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': r, 'col': c} for r, c in m_pos]
    result = action(actions)
    
    # Check if level completed
    if result.get('level_completed') or result.get('done'):
        print(f"Level completed after batch {i+1}!")
        break
    
    # Print M positions after each batch
    seg = current_frame.segmentation
    m_positions = []
    for node in seg['nodes']:
        if node['color'] == 'M' and node['pixels'] == 4:
            r = min(p[0] for p in node['boundary'])
            c = min(p[1] for p in node['boundary'])
            m_positions.append((r, c))
    print(f"After batch {i+1}: M at {sorted(m_positions)}")
